They escorted me back to Zvonko Santic's house again, and they told me that I would be in a kind of house arrest, that I mustn't leave the house because they would control the area, and this is something that I noticed anyway, I could notice their presence around the building, so that I was taken back to Zvonko Santic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: So on the 13th of May, you were finally able to leave Vitez, and since then, Mr. Zeco, have you had the chance to regain possession of your house?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No. I was not able to go back home until perhaps a month ago. Now I can tell you that I have submitted all the necessary papers and requests and even taken the matter to court to regain possession of my property.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: As far as you know, Mr. Zeco, how many Muslims from the area of Rijeka remained in that area after the facts that you have just described?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: All in all, in the urban area which was under the control of the HVO, I know that only between 90 and 100 Muslims stayed on in the area under HVO control in Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lopez-Terres, the witness told us that he went back to his house a month ago. Does that mean that his claims have been fruitful?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: Mr. Zeco, could you give us a more precise answer regarding the results of your claims?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Most recently I got in touch with various humanitarian organisations or, rather, organisations providing legal assistance and which are trying to assist refugees and exiled persons to recover their property. Since that is my wish and my desire and intention, to recover my property and to go back, a month ago I tried to do something in that area. I submitted the request to the municipal authority six months ago, in writing, but I received no answer to those requests. However, now, with the assistance and intervention of these institutions which are participating in dealing with these problems, I was counselled that I should go and try and get in touch with the people who are currently living in my house, and that is what I did. I was not able to enter; they didn't let me go inside. But they said until they have resolved their own problems, they would not let me enter. I didn't argue. I left it to the official authorities to deal with the problem and to make it possible for me to recover my property.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President, for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If it please the Court, Mr. Kovacic wanted to go first, but he's not ready at this point. This witness was sprung on us, so with the Court's permission, I'll take the lead here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Zeco.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sir, my name is Stephen Sayers, and I represent Dario Kordic. I'll try to be brief in the questions that I have for you this afternoon, sir. I understand, sir, that you have given a statement to the Prosecution's investigators in July of 1995. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That statement was given at the Ministry of the Interior in Sarajevo; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Where was it given, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I gave my statement in Zenica, in the building -- in the municipal building of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And you gave another statement to the Prosecution, I believe, in January of 1997, sir; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Quite possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I believe that you testified in the Blaskic case over the course of two days, on September the 25th and 26th, 1997, two years ago?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Throughout 1991 and 1992, sir, it's true, is it not, that you were actually active in civic matters in the Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I became active in the Vitez municipality; that is to say, involved in solving the problems that had arisen in July 1992. That's when I started.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Prior to that time, you had actually been a member of the municipal staff for civil defence; is that not true, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I was otherwise, throughout the period before the conflict and in the former system as well, I was always in the municipal staff for civil defence. I always worked there, and I covered the subject matter of the protection of livestock animals and property.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In that capacity, I believe, you had attended various seminars and training courses that equipped you with the knowledge to develop plans for the defence of the civilian population in the event of a military attack; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Throughout that time, a long time ago, I went through all forms of education at the level of the republic, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as it was then, and even on a federal level as well, of federal importance. Once again, with regard to the protection of civilians, property, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You've already told the Trial Chamber that you sat on the war presidency formed by the Muslim people in January of 1993 as the commander at the municipal headquarters of the civilian defence staff; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So I take it that you brought to the job, if you like, some personal experience and training that equipped you to perform your duties in that capacity; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just a few general questions about the area that you lived and travelled around in as a veterinarian, sir, primarily the Vitez/Rijeka area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In the map that you were shown, which was marked as Z2767, that you marked up in the case against General Blaskic, this map basically shows the area where you discharged your responsibilities as a veterinary practitioner; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Could I please ask you to repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, it was probably not as clear as it could be. Let me just ask you to take a look at the map that you were shown by counsel for the Prosecution. It was marked as Z2767. Would it be fair to say that this map basically shows the area where you practised as a vet in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Occasionally, sir, as I understand it, but only occasionally, you would be required to venture out as far as Travnik to the west and Busovaca to the southeast; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes, and related to performing our jobs as vets, we cooperated; that is to say, we were institutionally linked as a work organisation in Busovaca, Vitez, Novi Travnik, Travnik. Administratively, we were integrated into a common service. Of course, every veterinary station had performed its own professional duties in the area it covered, but when the occasion arose, we even worked in the areas of other municipalities, so that this area of the Lasva River Valley is very well known to me. On several occasions over the years, I would replace my colleague, Pero Kordic, when he went on holiday. I would replace him and perform the duties of a veterinary surgeon in the Busovaca municipality, so that this area of Busovaca, Vitez, Novi Travnik, Travnik, is fairly well known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. You drove around in your vehicle to perform services for various people in your municipality, I take it, throughout the years of 1992 and up to the outbreak of the fighting in April of 1993; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: As you've previously stated to the Trial Chamber, your face was well-known and your job was well-known by pretty much everybody that you came across in the area; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, it would be also fair to say, sir, that Vitez has a primarily farming and agrarian economy for the people who live in the outlying villages; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: With the exception of the two explosives and ammunition factories actually located in the town of Vitez itself, the Vitezit factory and the Slobodan Princip Seljo factory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You would also agree that Vitez was a vital transit area between the rural and the urban areas; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, it was on the main road between the towns of Banja Luka and Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: An extremely important road in Central Bosnia; would you not agree, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me just turn very briefly to the circumstances under which the republic was founded, and I won't spend too much time on this, sir. Would it be fair to say that the Bosnian Serbs boycotted the referendum that was held on the independence of the country on February the 28th and March the 1st of 1992?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes, you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But the Croats who lived in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Muslims too voted overwhelmingly in favour of independence of the country in that referendum, did they not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The republic was actually founded on March the 6th of 1992 as an independent country; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Within one month, sir, your country was embroiled in a terrible civil war, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, the Serbs had, I believe, surrounded and attacked the town of Mostar on March the 16th of 1992; does that sound about correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: As far as dates go, I did not pay any great attention to the dates, but probably it was thereabouts, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. Do you recall that within a month of the founding of the country, the capital, Sarajevo, was attacked, surrounded, and besieged by forces belonging to your Bosnian Serb countrymen and also by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I think that -- yes. Yes, but I personally could accept that that was done by the Yugoslav army, the Yugoslav army; that is to say, that the army did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, would it be fair to say that there had been large numbers, very large numbers of refugees flooding into the Lasva Valley from the north, from the east, and also from the west as a result of offensives launched by Bosnian Serbs against their fellow countrymen?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Essentially, sir, in the spring, if you like, of 1993, you'd been lucky, if you like, in the Lasva Valley because there had essentially been no attacks in the Lasva Valley by your Bosnian Serb countrymen against you and your Croat countrymen; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: The Vitez area was saved from a general attack, yes, that's right, but in the immediate vicinity of the Lasva River Valley; that is to say, the area of Vlasic, Zenica, where there had been an instance of that aggression in the vicinity of Vitez, and so this, of course, was reflected and had an effect on the situation in the Vitez area. That was the object of organising the defence, the army's defence, and the HVO units which were in the initial stages, they had a joint -- they were jointly organised by way of defending the region. Yes, that's true. And Vitez, from that aggressor, let us say the Serb aggressor, led by the army of the former Yugoslavia, Vitez luckily escaped an attack. It was not attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's true, though, isn't it, sir, that the subject of needing to arm in self-defence was a subject that was discussed very frequently by both you, the Muslims, and by the Croats in the Vitez area after the attacks in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: In that period of time, I was not directly engaged in activities of that kind. I was still -- I was just informed and kept abreast of everything. I kept abreast of everything, but I did not have any activities. I was not involved in the first half of 1992, but I did receive information as to the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You have explained to the Trial Chamber the circumstances under which the HVO basically took over the organs of the municipal government in Vitez in approximately June of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: About a month later, you and your colleagues set up a body by the name of "The Coordination Committee for the Protection of Muslims"; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you were elected to that body, sir, were you not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, we know all this. The witness has agreed and given evidence about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would it be safe to say with respect to the civilian police, about which you've given evidence, Mr. Zeco, that it was your opinion that they were essentially ineffective in Vitez when it came to assaults performed upon you by members of the military?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I did not say that they were ineffective, because the chief of MUP, Mirko Samija, who explained that to me, given the prevailing circumstances, they could not conduct an investigation as they would have liked to have conducted one, and Mirko Samija himself insisted and even the next day called me and told me that, at all costs, I should go to Travnik, to the hospital there for a medical examination which would ascertain an objective finding, so that he would have this finding, and when the time was ripe for this, an investigation would go through. I believed him, in view of the developments, and I accepted that state of affairs and those facts. Those are the observations that I have to make in respect of that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just a few questions about Mirko Samija. He was the chief of civilian police in the Vitez municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And he was a Croat, sir, was he not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Who was the chief of the military police in your municipality at that time?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I think that at that time, before Mirko Samija, the chief of police was Pero Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. With respect to the assaults that were launched upon you by the members of the HVO military, did you ever make a complaint to the military police, to Mr. Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No, I personally did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Turning now to the October 1992 conflict in your municipality that you described to the Trial Chamber, you were aware that the Bosnian Serbs were launching a violent attack upon the town of Jajce throughout October of 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, sir, that the townspeople of Jajce were in a desperate way during that month, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand you. Could you ask the question again, the latter half?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I'd be happy to. Would you agree with me that the townspeople in Jajce, who were subjected to the violent attack by Bosnian Serbs in October of 1992, were in a pretty desperate way?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The town of Jajce was actually captured by the Bosnian Serbs on October the 24th, was it not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, stepping back to October the 19th and 20th, Mr. Zeco, there had not --

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: -- there had not been any previous armed fighting, as far as you were aware, between the Muslims and the Croats in the Lasva Valley, had there?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Which period? Up until which period, do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: When the roadblock was placed on the main road at Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No, there wasn't; although up until then, on several occasions, there were incidents of various kinds where the members of the HVO encountered members of the army and disarmed them, if we can call this incidents or -- this is what happened up until then, in the course of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. So would it be fair to say that when the roadblock was erected at Ahmici on October the 19th, that was the first time in your municipality that a large number of Muslims had confronted Croats, armed and impeding their access to the main supply route at Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I personally was not a part of situations like that. I was not involved. All I know is that it was a question of passage for the military units; whereas there was no other impediment to anybody else's access. So it was only this event of the 19th of October that took place, and it was then that that area became involved, that area of Ahmici. I don't know that there was the inclusion of any other units but that it was only at a local level, at the level of the village of Ahmici. That was that particular incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The last question on this subject: That's the first time, as far as you're aware, in the Lasva Valley that Muslims forces stopped an HVO troop convoy at gunpoint; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Indeed, I think that you would agree that that was the perfect point at which to place a roadblock because that controlled the communications west to east along that road; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Well, the whole term, the Lasva Valley, is a narrow area, this whole space, so that it is an area of Ahmici, a narrow area which could be placed under control. So from that aspect, we can accept that definition, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'd like to give the Trial Chamber just a visual image of what the geography and the hills are like around Ahmici. As you are driving from Vitez to Ahmici, sir, it's pretty obvious that the land on either side is fairly open and somewhat flat until you get to the Catholic cemetery, and then the hills basically become very steep on either side at that point, don't they?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: You mean -- well, Ahmici itself, Ahmici, the settlement, that area, Santici, it is a broader area. So it's the broad area from the Kaonik region, which is exceptionally narrow, and that is the space between Busovaca and the Vitez municipality. So that is that part, that region, whereas Ahmici lies in another region, where it is broader, a broader space, so that more easterly -- from the military aspects, a more narrow area would be in the easterly part, which could be placed under military control and supervision, whereas Ahmici, the Ahmici area itself, is rather broad. But yes, as far as communications go, with the road, the roadblock was placed precisely at that section of the road. But there was breadth in the area as you go farther on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me just read to you a little piece of your 1995 statement that was given in July concerning this subject. You said that "We made a decision to make a barricade at Ahmici. This was the best place to have communicational control of the roads." Do you still agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No, I don't agree. In deciding upon erecting a roadblock, I personally did not take part in that, in any discussions or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me just move on to one other subject that you addressed with the Trial Chamber, and that was the decision made by the Muslim forces to relocate their headquarters from one building in Vitez to Stari Vitez; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I remember that incident when that situation occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I believe that the new headquarters was set up in the fire station right next to the mosque in Stari Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No. I know very well that after the headquarters was transferred from the secondary school centre, that the headquarters were located in the house of Cazim Patkovic. After that time, and that is to say immediately before it was transferred, it was first the Cazim Patkovic house, and after a certain amount of time it was in the fire brigade station, and then to another locality, a firm which collected waste products, so that was where it was afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've described the establishment of the war presidency by the Muslim political leadership in Vitez in January of 1993; do you remember that? Isn't it true that the war presidency had to be set up by a municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes, that the war presidency was formed on the basis of statements from delegates, members of the municipal assembly, and that the necessary number of deputies was required, and with their signature and acquiescence, they set up a war presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Two other members of the war presidency in addition to yourself, I take it, were Sefkija Dzidic, the military commander of the forces in Stari Vitez; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Also Saban Mahmutovic, who was the chief of the police on the Muslim side; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So as of January 1993, you essentially had two parallel governments; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: One Croat, one Muslim, operating side by side at the same time and in the same municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Including two separate police forces and two separate police stations?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Later on there was the establishment of joint co-operation and joint action. What we wanted to do was to link this up, and I know that at that time, when it came to a determination of functions, we would contact the other side, so to speak, that is to say, the Croat side. I know that when I wanted to set up co-operation and the work of the civil defence units, then we had a joint meeting and established a sort of joint body for civil defence, a municipal body, so that on the Croatian side, the Croatian side nominated Rudo Strbac, appointed him for civilian matters, and for military matters, they appointed Marko Krezic. At the time he was defence secretary for the Vitez municipality. On the other side, so to speak, I was in charge of civilian matters, so that we tried to have a joint body for civil defence purposes and activities, whereas Suljo Kalco, Sulejman Kalco was his name, he was in charge of military affairs on behalf of the army, so that in a way, this was to have been, at that time, teamwork on the part of the civil defence teams. There was close co-operation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Zeco, I'm going to interrupt you. If anybody wants any more detail, they'll ask. If you would keep your answers as short as possible, we will be able to get on quickly and will finish your evidence as soon as we can. Yes, have you got very much more, Mr. Sayers?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would think about 20 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What you're saying, Mr. Zeco, is that from the perspective of the Muslim leadership, there was a civilian arm and a military arm; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The same thing was true with respect to the HVO government, wasn't it? You had a civilian administration in Vitez and then a military arm too?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The name of the head of the civilian government in Vitez was Ivica Santic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, the mayor, was the brother of Zvonko Santic, the gentleman who gave you lodging in May of 1993; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Then the military arm of the HVO, if you like, in Vitez, was headed by whom?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: The military component in Vitez was led by Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever meet Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I believe that I recall that Blaskic was the commander of units for the Central Bosnia area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: On the subject of loyalty oaths, it's true, isn't it, that only about ten or so people actually lost their jobs as a result of refusal to sign these oaths?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I guess it is possible. As far as I know, those who had some kind of a position and who did not sign, I know that several of those lost their jobs in the Vitez municipality organs, whereas while this issue was being considered, that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it's true that only about ten or so people lost their jobs, and that is true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You did not lose your job, did you, as a veterinary practitioner, if you like?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: The veterinary station was a public institution with its own rules and regulations. It was only controlled by the municipal authorities indirectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You didn't lose your job, did you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Nor did your wife, did she?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, four years ago, you gave a statement to the Prosecution where you stated that you believed that Mr. Skopljak was actually in charge of the civilian government in Vitez. Is that still your view?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: That who was heading the government, did you mention?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Pero Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No. The head of the government, that was the HVO government, and it was headed at that time by the mayor, Ivica Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me just read you a statement from page 3 of your July 12 and 14, 1995, statement. You say, quote: "The representatives of the Croats were Skopljak, Pero," and some other names. "The mayor was Santic Ivica, but my opinion was that in actuality, the man in charge was Skopljak Pero, because he was in command of the HVO. The official representative of the civil authorities was Santic Ivica, but the HVO and its leader, Skopljak, had the real power. It was so obvious that Skopljak Pero was in charge." Now, do you remember making that statement?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: In that sense, yes, that statement of mine is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So it was actually Mr. Skopljak who was in charge of the civilian government and not Mr. Santic, is what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No. No, officially, in an official sense, Ivica Santic was the representative of authority in the Vitez municipality government. But Pero Skopljak was also in the government, and his influence was crucial and significant in resolving all types of situations which had arisen. That is how my statement was framed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me turn to another subject, which is your conversation with Mr. Kordic's father, Pero Kordic, in January of 1993. That conversation occurred after fighting had broken out in Busovaca in that month; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the Muslim forces in Busovaca were responsible for launching an attack on that town in January of 1993, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I did not analyse the situation that developed. I only know that in Busovaca, the legal authority was suspended and the power was taken over by the HVO. It established its own authority in the territory of the Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you hear about the massacre of 12 Croats at the village of Dusina on the 26th of January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I have heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you spoke to Mr. Kordic after that massacre, didn't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes, we spoke after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Turning, sir, to the testimony that you gave regarding the fighting that broke out on April the 16th, as I understand it, you were arrested by HVO soldiers dressed in combat gear and camouflage on that morning; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were taken about 20 metres, if you like, from your house to the veterinarian station and basically detained in your office; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: It's more like 50 to 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you remember that the night before, you had actually recommended calling a meeting of the war presidency to discuss the elaboration of plans to protect Muslims in the case of an HVO attack?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, on this map that we've been looking at, this photocopy, Rijeka appears to be about one kilometre or less from Kruscica; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Well, it is -- the area of Kruscica is kind of set in, that area of Kruscica where the local commune of Rijeka is, around the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Specifically, my house and the veterinarian station are about 500 to 1.000 metres, as the crow flies, to Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: On April the 16th of 1993, Kruscica was the headquarters of the 325th Mountain Brigade of the Muslim forces, commanded by Sifet Sivro; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I believe that at that time, the commander was Dzenanovic, Esad Dzenanovic, on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But the headquarters of the 325th Mountain Brigade were located in Kruscica on April the 16th; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, you were not maltreated in any way when you were taken to the Hotel Vitez on May the 8th; is that correct, sir? This is after the military plans had been found in your car.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Following your release from the Hotel Vitez, it's true that Dr. Mujezinovic wrote you a falsified diagnosis of heart problems, and that resulted in your transport to Travnik hospital; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I do have a heart condition, for your information. I did have four bypasses, and Dr. Mujezinovic was my physician. In 1990, I was operated on, my heart. So, in fact, I am a heart patient, if you will. So nothing was really forged, but we made an agreement because I was in some sort of detention, and we agreed that he would help me to be moved to the Travnik hospital, which was done. But not as a forgery; it had to do with a real situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I don't mean to belabour the point, Mr. Zeco, but on page 8 of the statement that you gave four years ago, here's what you said: You were able to arrange for Dr. Mujezinovic "... to give me a falsified paper stating that I needed treatment at hospital, and it was because of this that I was taken to Travnik hospital on the 13th of May, 1993, and that is how I escaped from Vitez." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: You cannot say that it was falsified. I forged -- I agreed that with Dr. Mujezinovic's help, I was transferred from Vitez to Travnik, and that was an arrangement that was made. But, indeed, in 1990, I had a heart surgery, I had four bypasses done then, and so I don't know about the word "falsified" or "forged." I do not agree with that wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But you do remember signing each page or initialling each page of the statement and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Sayers, we've got the point, so far as it helps us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I don't mean to beat it to death, Your Honour, and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Is it true that your veterinarian assistant was stopped, sir, shortly before the April 1993 conflict and was discovered to have arms in his car?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes. This was Cazim Patkovic, who was a member of the army, and he helped out at the veterinarian station. He had been a member of the TO at that time. I did not follow their activities; they had their own tasks and their own business. I know that as a member of the TO, that is, of the BH army, he had his military activities, and I know of an incident when his car was taken and a certain amount of ammunition was found. I did go to the municipality to have that car returned. It is a fact that this did happen, but he was a member of the Territorial Defence, that is, a member of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let's turn to the subject of the defence plans that were discovered in your car. You'd actually temporarily disabled the car by disconnecting cables in it, had you not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes, I did so every night because the situation had already been created where cars were disappearing from garages, and this was a measure that I took to prevent that, so that the car could not be started.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. These plans that were discovered in your car actually described what would be done in the event that fighting should break out or that there should be an attack in certain areas; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: For example, if there were to be an attack on the village that you lived in, Rijeka, there would be an evacuation of the civilian population to the headquarters --

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: -- of the 325th Mountain Brigade in Kruscica; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No, not to the brigade command, in any event, but in the area where there was some natural shelter, where the civilian population could be sheltered, and this was the area of Kruscica, which is hilly, which is forested. It had nothing to do with the brigade command being located in Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The civilians who lived in the Kolonija section of Vitez would be evacuated to the town of Gacice or the village of Gacice just to the southeast of Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes, and then again, this is an area which would have the same natural features, I mean, the one in Gacice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Similarly, your plans also contemplated what would happen in the event of an attack on the villages of Santici and Nadioci; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Again certain tasks were supposed to be assigned. Certain people should have been tasked with the protection of the civilian population in that area and do everything that was necessary. In all the areas where the Muslim population lived, there were a number of persons who were tasked with the protection of the civilian population which was threatened in these built-up areas where they lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just to get back to the question that I asked you, sir, specifically, your defence plans dealt with what would happen to the civilian population in the event of an HVO attack on the villages of Santici and Nadioci; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, if I might just ask the usher to put Z2767 on the ELMO, I'd just like you to point out where Santici and Nadioci are. If you could use the pointer, sir.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You are now pointing to Santici or Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Nadioci [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: This is Santici [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Could you just point out where Ahmici is, please?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Between Nadioci and Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Could you tell the Trial Chamber what the plans called for in the event that Ahmici were to be attacked?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: The area of Ahmici, Ahmici and the surrounding area, was supposed to be secured in terms of protection of the civilian population so that the population in this area would be safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. So your plans actually contemplated what would occur in the event of an HVO attack on the village of Ahmici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes. Since there were natural conditions which were conducive to protection, that if there were any combat to take place there, that the population around Ahmici would be protected, and the population did have a potential of being protected in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You had actually devised these plans after consultation with the military commanders, Sulejman Kalco and Sifet Sivro; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: They took it upon themselves to consider this plan from the military standpoint and to do their part; that is, to give their own solutions from the military standpoint. So they were in charge of this military side of this issue, to find the right solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's because by this time, by April the 16th of 1993, it was obvious to you and your colleagues, both civil and military, of the war presidency that conflicts between the HVO and the Muslim forces in the Lasva Valley were inevitable; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: After -- that was the assumption given the unfolding of the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, you mentioned the village of Vrhovine. I only have one question for you on this. All of the Croats who used to live in this village were cleaned out of the town in 1993, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Personally, I don't know that, with the exception of further out towards Nadioci, that there were any Croat families living in Vrhovine. In the village of Vrhovine itself, there were no Croats, but to the northeast, I know that that's where Mirko Samir's family is from, so there may have been some Croatian families there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Zeco, I'm going to interrupt you. Now, Mr. Sayers, I wish to finish your cross-examination today, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Believe me, Your Honour, I do too, and I think that I have about another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Turning to the truck bomb incident, sir, everything that you know about that incident you were told by others; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: What I just said a moment ago is what Zeljko Matkovic had told me, is what I knew. He provided the information about the bomb, so he was the one who transmitted this information to all of us who were detained in the veterinary station, and this is what I was referring to when I said what I knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And I think we agree on this, though: What you know about that is derived exclusively from what you were told by other people; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the same thing goes with respect to casualties that you described in the trench-digging incidents, the people that were supposedly shot or died during that. You didn't see any of these people shot yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: This is mostly on the basis of people who were sent out to dig and who had come back from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But the point is, what you've told the Trial Chamber is essentially what you were told by other people, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes, on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you also gave some testimony with respect to stories about a threat to blow up the Dubravica school in the event of a continued assault by Muslim forces; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that on the 22nd of April, 1993, there was actually a cease-fire agreement that was signed by General Sefer Halilovic, Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic, and countersigned by General Philippe Morillon and by John Pierre Thebault from the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: At that time, I did not know this. While I was in the camp -- that is, throughout the period which I spent in detention -- I did not know of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But all you knew is that somehow the fighting around the school stopped on or around April the 22nd, 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Just a few final questions for you, sir. Were you aware that the town of Travnik was attacked by Muslim forces on June the 8th and captured on June the 12th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: On 8 June? I did not have such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you aware that the town of Kakanj had been attacked on June the 9th by Muslim forces and captured on June the 13th of 1993?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that large numbers of refugees, Croat refugees, were the result of the Travnik fighting and the Kakanj fighting and the capture of those two cities by Muslim forces in the early summer of 1993?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I know this fact, that there was a large number of Croat refugees in that area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you know that the town of Fojnica had been attacked and captured by Muslim forces in July of 1939, and that resulted in a large efflux of Croat refugees as well?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: With respect to the towns which you mentioned, my understanding was that those areas had been defended. Because in these areas -- and I know this because I live in the wide area of Zenica -- I know that it was the Croats from those areas who voluntarily and under other people's influence had left, and that the legal authorities had stayed on the ground. I know this because I am in such an area, because currently, I reside in the Zenica region.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Finally, were you aware that the town of Vares had been attacked and captured on November the 1st and 2nd, 1993, and that resulted in about 7.000 Croat refugees leaving the town?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, that this also happened in the territory of Vares municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: My final questions for you, Mr. Zeco, are these: Is it true that in your house in Rijeka, right now, Croat refugees from somewhere live?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know where they are refugees from, sir?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: I know. In my home, until recently, in my house, there were Ivica Livancic, who is a Croat from Dubravica, and even to date, I have an official document from the Vitez municipality, so I received a document from the people who currently are using my house, that they had paid 1.600 German marks, that they had paid that money in order to be allowed to move into my house, and now they have officially stated that they refused to leave the house because they did not recognise any of Westendorp's laws. I have this document in my possession. This was a document that was drafted officially in the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do I take it, sir, that you now live in Zenica, the city of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the house that you currently live in, who was that formerly owned by?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: It was a social apartment. Formerly it was occupied by a person who lived [sic] in a local transport company, and he filed a request to be given back his apartment, and I was then asked to come and give an official statement. I did accept that and recognised that he should come back, but that my problem should also be resolved, because right now I have a provisional decision which allows me to stay in this apartment with my wife while my children have left Bosnia and have moved to the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Finally, sir, what was the ethnicity of the person who used to live in your apartment before you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD ZECO
utterances.text: It was -- the person was of Croatian ethnic background, and the other persons who are there are also ethnic Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kovacic, tomorrow morning, for your cross-examination, I hope you can be expeditious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tomorrow afternoon, it's pointed out, not tomorrow morning. Half past two tomorrow afternoon. I hope you can be expeditious, so that we can get on to another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, you've got 24 hours to prepare --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- and sharpen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One point about the transcript. I see that days 53 to 56 seem to be missing; that today is described as day 54. It should be day 57. No doubt that's being attended to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 4.25 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 14th day of September, 1999, at 2.30 p.m.
